Goosie media journey

Served over HTTP so the browser's own download pipeline, cookie jar and address policy are all in the path. Nothing here uses a file: URL.

1. Native controls, no script

Play, pause, seek and mute must all work from the painted control bar alone. This element has no JavaScript attached to it at all.

2. Scripted controls

The buttons call the media API. play() is called from a real click handler, which is a trusted gesture; a setTimeout calling it must be refused with NotAllowedError, and the log below says which happened.

readyState-paused-
currentTime-duration-
videoWidth-videoHeight-
muted-currentSrc-






  
3. Clipped by an ancestor

  
The dashed box is 120px tall and the video is 180px, so the control bar
  is cut in half. The controls must stay where the element puts them — they used to be
  laid out against the clipped rectangle, which made them slide as the page scrolled.

This one names a file that does not exist. It must report an error
  rather than sit there looking like a video that has not started.
